page: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is a low-footprint virtual server built on the ARM64 architecture using first-generation AWS Graviton Cortex-A72 processors running at 2.3 GHz. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU across 1 physical core without hyperthreading. It is provisioned with 2.0 GB of memory, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache architecture consists of 32 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache, with no L3 cache present. Cryptographic workloads benefit from hardware AES acceleration, though x86 instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are not supported.

Synthetic benchmark results reflect an entry-level performance profile suited to basic workloads. Single-core CPU evaluation via stress-ng achieved a score of 1449.88, positioning it in the middle performance tier for single-threaded processing. Multi-core performance matches single-core due to the single vCPU configuration. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 386.0, a multi-core score of 384.0, and a software compilation score of 497.0 using Clang. PassMark CPU testing logged a score of 381.78, while memory bandwidth tests measured 35.11 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 10.43 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Application-level metrics recorded 0.47 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 0.48 GB/sec.

Without attached local NVMe storage and with a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps, the instance relies on remote EBS storage for disk persistence. The single-core dedicated vCPU model combined with 2.0 GB of memory makes the server a cost-effective option for light, ARM-native execution environments. Appropriate workload fits include lightweight containerized microservices, basic web applications, small-scale CI/CD build runners, and testing pipelines for ARM64 software builds.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is an entry-level ARM-based cloud server powered by a first-generation AWS Graviton Cortex-A72 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it provides 1 dedicated vCPU, 1 physical core, 2.0 GB of system memory, 32 KB L1d cache, and 2 MB L2 cache. The ARM64 architecture includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography but lacks x86-specific vector extensions. Benchmarks reflect entry-level performance, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1449.88, a Geekbench single-core score of 386.0, and 0.47 million Redis SET operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 10.43 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 0.48 GB/sec. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. Positioned as a low-overhead, compute-aligned ARM resource, the a1.medium offers reasonable resource efficiency for lightweight ARM-native microservices, continuous integration runners, basic web servers, and software build environments.
